args.message:
Fix money rounding to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

round_money() was importing and applying ROUND_HALF_UP despite the
docstring (and FIN-212) specifying banker's rounding. This caused
the nightly test failure in tests/test_money.py (e.g. 2.665 rounded
to 2.67 instead of 2.66). Switch the quantize call to
ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix money rounding to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
`src/money.py`'s `round_money()` claimed to implement banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but was actually using `ROUND_HALF_UP`. This broke the nightly build's `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`, which expects:
- `2.675` → `2.68` (rounds up to even)
- `2.665` → `2.66` (rounds down to even)

## Changes
- Imported `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
- Used it in the `quantize()` call.

## Testing
CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passes, including the previously failing banker's-rounding test.
